title: sse: fix streaming chunking and framing issues (partial JSON, delimiters, token ordering)
author: Ava Lin
description: Summary: Fixes several interrelated SSE streaming issues that caused downstream parsers to receive partial/invalid JSON events, missing delimiters, and out-of-order token/event emission. Motivation: Customers reported flaky streaming behavior for long responses and tool/function-calling payloads where the client could not reliably reassemble JSON objects from SSE events. This caused application-level parse errors and regressions in OpenAI-compatible streaming clients. Changes: 1) Introduce a stable framing layer that marks event boundaries and preserves token order across async buffers. 2) Ensure token-level partial JSON pieces are buffered per-stream and only emitted when syntactically complete OR when a delimiting event is required (e.g., end_of_json). 3) Fix a race between the chunk aggregator and the SSE writer that could drop trailing delimiters for rapid-fire model outputs. 4) Add explicit delimiter insertion for multi-chunk JSON outputs and normalize the client-facing SSE event names to be backwards compatible with the OpenAI compatibility layer. 5) Add tests: unit coverage for the chunker, integration test simulating slow clients and bursty model streams, and an e2e example in redwood-openai-compat that validates OpenAI-style parsers. Backwards compatibility: This change keeps the existing SSE event names but stabilizes ordering and framing; no user-visible API changes expected. Rollout: Feature-flag gated for 2 days in staging, then enabled by default. Related: Linked Linear items ENG-3271, ENG-3304. CI: flakey streaming test fixed and rerun. See CI details below.
